clue.text: Father stilted as a result of grub being laid in cornfield?

definitions.text: as a result of grub being laid in cornfield?

parts.note: daddy is a familiar word for a father
someone stilted, raised up on stilts, has long legs

explanation.surface: A father walks stiffly on account of some food buried in a field of wheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, but it is the larva: the crane-fly's leatherjacket grub lives in field soil, and the long-legged adult emerges from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly develops from a leatherjacket larva living in the soil of fields, so the adult insect is the result of that larva.

clue.text: Plant producing poison requires energy given to fresh action

indicators.note: fresh means made anew, so the letters of action are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A poisonous plant needs a new burst of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges ACTION into ACONIT, and E for energy is given to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood, the source of a deadly alkaloid, is the plant known by this name.

clue.text: A low cart with a 3ft back

indicators.note: back asks for the word for three feet to be read from its end to its start

parts.note: a yard is three feet

explanation.surface: A squat wagon with a tailboard three feet high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the rear of the cart, but it turns YARD round.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer's heavy flat wagon without sides is a classic low cart.

clue.text: Coming to rest in Mrs Bardell's Dickensian house?

definitions.meaning: a bullet or bone that sticks fast somewhere is said to be settling there
Mrs Bardell is Mr Pickwick's landlady in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers, who lets rooms to tenants

explanation.surface: Settling down to stay at a house from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Bardell, in The Pickwick Papers, keeps rooms for paying tenants, so her house is a place of rented rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodge means to become fixed in place, and rented rooms are accommodation of that name.

clue.text: True, ten frisky squirrels love one

indicators.note: frisky means lively and playful, so the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: It is true that ten playful squirrels adore something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisky' looks like a description of the squirrels, but it mixes up TRUE and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Squirrels gather hazelnuts and the like, so a tree bearing nuts is a favourite of theirs.

clue.text: A Northern pastoralist taking circuit quietly

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A northern herdsman makes a quiet round of his land.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer-herding Sami people of Arctic Scandinavia were long called by this name.

clue.text: Assembled in knots

definitions.meaning: a knot is a small cluster of people, so in knots means in clusters

explanation.definitionFit: Gathered people form clusters, and a knot of people is one such small cluster.

clue.text: Is shocking music piped from it?

definitions.text: Is shocking music piped from it?

parts.words: Is shocking music piped from it?
parts.note: shocking suggests an electric shock and piped suggests organ pipes, so the instrument powered by mains current is meant

explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument powered by mains current produces piped sound and could, in theory, give its player a jolt.

clue.text: Gastric old men ill-treated, but please don't spread it around

indicators.note: ill-treated means handled badly, so the letters are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: Elderly men with sick stomachs are asked not to pass on their illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-treated' rearranges GASTRIC and OLD MEN together, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cold with a running nose is an infection everyone asks the sufferer not to pass on.

clue.text: Tip of foot reflectively inserted into fat dancer's garment

indicators.note: inserted into says one piece goes inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: reflectively suggests a mirror image, so the word for the foot's tip is read backwards

parts.note: the toe is the tip of the foot

explanation.surface: A dancer's tights get a mirror-check of the toe and a bit of padding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat' looks like a description of the dancer, but it is the cooking fat that holds the turned-round toe; 'reflectively' does the turning and 'inserted into' the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting one-piece costume is what ballet dancers and gymnasts wear for practice.

clue.text: Paint put on before going outdoors?

definitions.text: Paint put on before going outdoors?

parts.words: Paint put on before going outdoors?
parts.note: the final layer of paint is put on last, and an overcoat is put on before going out of doors

explanation.definitionFit: The final layer of paint and an overcoat worn outside both go by this name.

clue.text: The company joining in when there's something to spend

explanation.surface: A firm joins in when there is money to spend.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of metal money is something you can spend in a shop.

clue.text: Lie about a moral quality

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Telling a lie about someone's moral character.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of strong moral fibre has character and backbone; the word means inner strength.

clue.text: He canvassed late Georgians in grip of Old English piety

indicators.note: in grip of says the word for piety is held inside the letters for Old English

parts.note: pi is a colloquial short form of pious, so it stands for piety

explanation.surface: A man went canvassing among elderly Georgians, gripped by old-fashioned piety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvassed' looks like electioneering but means painted on canvas: John Opie was a Cornish portrait painter of the late Georgian period.
explanation.definitionFit: John Opie painted portraits of people of the late eighteenth century, the later Georgian era.

clue.text: Married women with singular views

indicators.note: singular means strange or odd, so the letters of views take an odd new order

explanation.surface: Married women with unusual opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like grammar, but it means odd and rearranges VIEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with a husband is his spouse; this is the plural.

clue.text: Very grey matter if it gets knocked out of 22

indicators.note: gets knocked out of says the word it is removed from the country's name

parts.note: the answer to 22 across, the old country

explanation.surface: It turns very grey if knocked out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' refers to the answer to 22 across; take IT out of that to leave the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is made of grey matter, so it is that matter in a very full sense.

clue.text: Reacting to the shock of winding up?

definitions.meaning: staggering or swaying after a blow or bad news
winding in a fishing line on a reel

explanation.surface: Responding to the shock of being wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is staggering from a blow; the other is winding a line in on a reel.

clue.text: A man belted by party member shows such dignity?

parts.note: a belted earl is a nobleman invested with a sword belt
a do is a party
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A nobleman in a sword belt, with a party politician, shows off his rank.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'belted earl' is a traditional phrase for a nobleman girded with a sword belt at his investiture.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity here is a rank or title, and the rank held by an earl is the dignity meant.

clue.text: Well pleased with what you've found inside?

definitions.meaning: the things contained in something, such as a box or a book

explanation.surface: Satisfied with what you discovered inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied is one sense; the other is what a container holds, stressed on the first syllable.

clue.text: A magic cure for the guitarist with no fingers?

definitions.meaning: a quack remedy promising to cure everything
a guitarist without fingers cannot sweep the strings, so there is no strumming

explanation.surface: A miracle remedy for a guitarist who has lost his fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits into two words: a fingerless guitarist can make NO STRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy sold as a cure-all; split in two it describes a fingerless guitarist's lack of strumming.

clue.text: Explosive material put more characters into great anguish

indicators.note: into says the jumbled letters are placed inside the explosive's abbreviation

parts.note: TNT is the abbreviation for trinitrotoluene, a high explosive

indicators.note: characters here means the letters of the word more, taken in a new order

explanation.surface: An explosive situation puts extra people into deep distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters, or characters, of 'more' are shuffled; 'into' then sets them inside the explosive's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe suffering of mind or body is the sense, as in the torment of waiting.

clue.text: I bait RN to bombard the old country .

indicators.note: bombard means to batter with shells, so the letters are blasted into a new order

parts.note: RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy, taken here just as letters

explanation.surface: I taunt the Royal Navy into shelling the old homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombard' scrambles I, BAIT and RN; 'the old country' is a fond name for the homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrants speak of their homeland as the old country, and for many that is the United Kingdom.

clue.text: So Benn, I construe, offers antidote to our cursed ills!

indicators.note: construe means interpret, so the letters are worked out in another order

explanation.surface: A politician named Benn is told his words offer a cure for our wretched troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construe' rearranges SO, BENN and I; Tony Benn was a British Labour politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A blessing is the opposite of a curse, so it counters ills that are cursed.

clue.text: Father reverses and gives cover to some enemies of C 24

indicators.note: reverses says the word for father is written back to front

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for a father
to hide something is to give it cover

explanation.surface: Dad backs up and shields some foes of the flower.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to 24 across, the flower; greenfly attack it, and this is a plural of the insect's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that infest rose bushes, so gardeners count them as foes of the flower.

clue.text: … and flower of England

parts.note: follows on from 22 across: the old country, and also its national flower

explanation.definitionFit: The red and white bloom of the Tudors is the national emblem of England.

clue.text: Railway network given plus mark

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the old national railway
and means plus, as in two and two

explanation.surface: The railway system gets an extra point.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, Britain's former nationalised railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name or an identifying burn on cattle is a mark of ownership or origin.

clue.text: Stylish part of a Zurich ice-show

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Elegant like a section of a skating show in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and fashionable is the sense; the word is borrowed from French.

clue.text: Ruin built up by some good I nursing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Ruin built up by some good I nursing': the reversed hidden UNDO (ODNU in 'goOD NUrsing') needs the stray 'I' gone, which neither printedClue nor setterError can express as a deletion; no scan to confirm.
annotationWithheld.clue: Ruin built up by some good I nursing

clue.text: A plucky spirit is supposed to play on it

definitions.text: A plucky spirit is supposed to play on it

parts.words: A plucky spirit is supposed to play on it
parts.note: plucky means plucking strings, and angels in heaven are pictured playing a stringed instrument

explanation.definitionFit: Angels in paintings and cartoons are shown plucking the strings of this large instrument.

clue.text: Order a Rontgen cooking apparatus

parts.note: R is the symbol for the roentgen, a unit of radiation
a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy an X-ray scientist a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays; the unit named after him has the symbol R.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order is to lay them out neatly in sequence.

clue.text: The disgraceful affair of Lady Teazle's schooling?

definitions.meaning: a shameful episode that causes public outrage
Lady Teazle is a character in Sheridan's play The School for ...

explanation.surface: A shameful episode from Lady Teazle's education.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Teazle appears in Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal, so her schooling is in gossip and disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A shameful affair causing public outrage, and the subject of the school in Sheridan's play title.

clue.text: The Governor, for example holds an urgent bag of mail

definitions.meaning: a governor holds a senior office, an example of a weighty position
letters that matter a great deal and must be delivered fast

explanation.surface: A governor has an urgent sack of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior office such as a governorship, and also mail of great consequence.
